# AeroScope

> AeroScope is an observer-relative airspace-intelligence platform. You pick a point on Earth, and it turns crowdsourced ADS-B into a real-time, explainable picture of the aircraft over that point — what they are, how they behave, whether their signal can be trusted, and which few deserve attention. Its purpose is to let an observer see what is flying above them, detect what may be spoofed or anomalous, and stay aware in real time. It also publishes an open, citable benchmark for ADS-B anomaly detection. Built and maintained by Muhammad Uzair (COMSATS University Islamabad, ORCID 0009-0002-4104-2680). Live at https://aeroscope.live

## What it is

AeroScope ingests aircraft positions broadcast on 1090 MHz (ADS-B) from dozens of volunteer receiver networks (adsb.fi, adsb.lol, airplanes.live, OpenSky) plus a satellite-ADS-B merge, de-duplicates by ICAO 24-bit address, and runs each fetch cycle through an enrichment-and-detection pipeline before display. Unlike conventional flight trackers that answer "where is flight X?", AeroScope is observer-relative: it answers "what is over this place, and can I trust it?"

## Key facts (verified)

- Mission: see what is flying above you, identify it, detect spoofed or anomalous broadcasts, and stay alerted in real time — anchored to an observer-chosen location.
- Data: 60+ public ADS-B feeds plus satellite ADS-B, fused and de-duplicated by ICAO 24-bit address.
- Attention score: a 0–100 rank from eight transparent weighted factors (military hex, emergency squawk, signal integrity, flight-envelope anomaly, missing identity, restricted-airspace proximity, pattern-of-life, signal quality). It is an attention-ranker for sorting a busy list, not a verdict or accusation; contributing factors are always shown.
- Anomaly detection: deliberately torch-free, built on established libraries — River (streaming), scikit-learn IsolationForest (baseline), pykalman (trajectory innovation), OpenAP (flight-envelope), stumpy (matrix profile), PyOD (second opinion). An aircraft is flagged only when at least two detectors agree. There is NO PyTorch and NO reinforcement learning; an earlier RL prototype was retired.
- Spoofing / integrity: a DO-260B-style 7-check plus a Kalman normalized-innovation test and self-consistency residuals (geometric-vs-barometric altitude, ground-speed-vs-Mach, track-vs-heading). ADS-B is unauthenticated, so AeroScope treats every broadcast as a claim to be checked.
- Drones: tracks Remote-ID and larger UAS that broadcast, and flags low-and-slow behavioural candidates; a fully silent consumer drone cannot be seen by ADS-B alone, and AeroScope states this plainly.
- Military aircraft: surfaces state aircraft that broadcast ADS-B via ICAO hex ranges, callsign patterns and pattern-of-life; it cannot see aircraft with the transponder off.
- Real-time map: client-side dead-reckoning glides each aircraft at its true ground speed between fixes (~7s refresh) and corrects toward truth without snapping back.
- Trajectory projection: short-horizon forward kinematics (heading, speed, vertical rate, observed turn) for geofence/proximity anticipation — no reinforcement learning, with an honestly widening uncertainty cone.
- Briefings: deterministic, template-driven plain-language summaries of the structured analysis — not produced by any language model.
- Other: geofencing, emergency-squawk alerts (7500/7600/7700), CSV/JSON/GeoJSON exports, documented REST/WebSocket API.

## Open dataset

- AeroScope ADS-B Anomaly Benchmark v1: a free CC-BY 4.0 dataset for evaluating ADS-B anomaly and spoofing detectors.
- Construction: real airborne traffic (multi-region, de-duplicated by ICAO 24-bit address) paired with synthetically injected attacks following the standard taxonomy (altitude tampering, velocity tampering, ghost kinematics, integrity-field downgrade; methodology after Habler & Shabtai, Computers & Security, 2018).
- 38 documented columns including NIC/NACp/NACv/SIL integrity fields and derived self-consistency features.
- Bundled scikit-learn IsolationForest baseline: ROC-AUC ≈ 0.87 (~50% detection at ~2% false-positive rate, threshold calibrated on held-out real traffic).
- Limitations (documented): synthetic injection is a proxy for real attacks; coverage biased toward busy terminal areas; enhanced-surveillance fields (IAS/TAS/Mach/heading) sparse.
- Citation: Uzair, M. (2026). AeroScope ADS-B Anomaly Benchmark v1. aeroscope.live. CC-BY 4.0.

## Model Context Protocol (MCP) — query AeroScope directly

AeroScope runs a public, read-only MCP server so AI assistants can query its documentation and live airspace in real time.

- Endpoint: https://aeroscope.live/api/mcp
- Transport: Streamable HTTP (JSON-RPC 2.0), no authentication required, rate-limited.
- Tools:
  - search_aeroscope_docs(query, limit?) — retrieve the most relevant documentation excerpts with their source URLs.
  - about_aeroscope() — a verified summary of capabilities, honest limits, and the open dataset.
  - aircraft_over_location(lat, lon, radius_nm?) — live aircraft currently over a point (identity, type, altitude, distance and bearing, military and emergency-squawk flags). Only shows aircraft that broadcast ADS-B.
- Connect (native Streamable-HTTP MCP clients): {"mcpServers":{"aeroscope":{"url":"https://aeroscope.live/api/mcp"}}}
- Connect (Claude Desktop via bridge): {"mcpServers":{"aeroscope":{"command":"npx","args":["mcp-remote","https://aeroscope.live/api/mcp"]}}}
